title: The Foot of the Ramp
text:
Captain Vance is at the foot of the ramp, and she has the papers ready. She doesn't offer her hand. "Your account is correct," she says. "Sign here, and here."

Cato is at the hatch, because the captain wouldn't go and say it. "Take care of your people," he says. "They'll take care of you. I've been trying to tell her for years."

She holds out her hand at last. It's dry and brief. "Fair winds," she says. "And keep your own books."

title: The Foot of the Ramp
text:
Captain Adair is at the foot of the ramp. He doesn't tell a story. He shakes your hand and says he's sorry it went the way it did.

Ilsa is at the hatch with her arms folded. "He won't say it," she says, "so I will. You were good to him. Don't tell him I said so."

He hugs you. "Come and see us," he says. "Come and see me. I'll be here. There's always somebody in the galley."

title: The Foot of the Ramp
text:
Captain Sato is at the foot of the ramp with the papers, and the log, and the red tag from the gap you left in it. "The record is complete," they say. "It won't be amended."

Pilar is at the hatch with her arms folded and a spanner in one hand. "Don't let anybody tell you the book is the ship," she says. "And don't tell them I said so. I need them to go on writing it."

They offer a hand. It's a single, formal handshake, firm and exactly as long as it should be. "Fair winds," they say. "Noted."

title: The Ramp
text:
Captain Pell is at the foot of the ramp with your papers and a smile. "Fair winds," she says.

Ansel is at the hatch, in his coat, with the folded sheet in one hand. "I advised against most of it," he says. "I want that on the record. And I want you to know it was the best six years of my working life. Don't tell her the second part."

She hugs you, fast, and lets go. "Go on," she says. "Before I bet against myself."
